description: Fideo Seco is a beloved Mexican comfort food, a savory dish of toasted vermicelli noodles simmered in a rich tomato-based sauce until dry and bursting with flavor. This humble yet satisfying 'dry pasta' offers a delightful texture and a warm, homey taste perfect for any family meal. It's a staple in Mexican households, often served as a side or a light main course, bringing a taste of tradition to your table.

instructions.title: Toast the Fideo Noodles
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Add the fideo noodles and toast them, stirring constantly, until they turn a deep golden brown, about 3-5 minutes. Be careful not to burn them. Remove the toasted fideo from the skillet and set aside on a plate, leaving any excess oil in the pan.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tomato Sauce Base
instructions.text: In a blender, combine the roughly chopped Roma tomatoes, white onion, and garlic cloves with 1/2 cup of the chicken broth. Blend until completely smooth. This should take about 1-2 minutes to ensure no large pieces remain. You want a fine puree for the sauce.

instructions.title: Cook the Tomato Sauce
instructions.text: Pour the blended tomato mixture into the same skillet where you toasted the fideo (add a little more oil if needed). Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sauce darkens in color and thickens, about 8-10 minutes. This step is crucial for developing a rich, deep flavor in your sauce.

instructions.title: Combine Fideo and Sauce
instructions.text: Return the toasted fideo noodles to the skillet with the cooked tomato sauce. Add the remaining 2 cups of chicken broth, salt, and black pepper. Stir everything together gently, making sure the fideo noodles are fully submerged in the liquid.

instructions.title: Simmer and Absorb
instructions.text: Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and let it simmer for about 15-20 minutes, or until the fideo noodles have absorbed almost all the liquid and are tender. Check periodically to ensure it's not sticking. If it gets too dry before the fideo is cooked, add a splash more broth.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once the fideo is cooked and the liquid is absorbed, remove the skillet from the heat and let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld and the fideo to finish absorbing any remaining moisture. Serve hot, garnished generously with a dollop of crema mexicana, crumbled queso fresco, and fresh chopped cilantro.

tips: For the perfect fideo texture, ensure you toast the noodles evenly to a deep golden brown before adding the sauce. This step is crucial for flavor and preventing sogginess, giving you that authentic 'seco' texture.

If you prefer a spicier kick, add one or two serrano or jalapeño peppers (stemmed) to your tomato sauce blend before pureeing. For a richer, more profound flavor, always use good quality chicken broth, or make your own.

Fideo Seco is best served immediately, garnished with a dollop of crema mexicana, crumbled queso fresco, and fresh cilantro. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheated gently on the stovetop with a splash of water or broth.
article:
In the tapestry of Mexican cuisine, Fideo Seco stands out as a humble yet utterly satisfying dish. This "dry noodle" preparation is a testament to resourceful cooking and a celebration of rich, savory goodness. If you crave a hearty, flavorful meal that’s easy to prepare and deeply satisfying, Fideo Seco might just be your new favorite go-to.

## What is Fideo Seco Dry Mexican Noodles?
Fideo Seco Dry Mexican Noodles is a dish featuring thin, short pasta (fideo) cooked in a rich, tomato-based sauce until almost all liquid evaporates. The "seco" (dry) refers to this method, where pasta absorbs the sauce, concentrating its flavors.

Its origins trace to Spanish influence in colonial Mexico, evolving from Spanish fideuá, a paella-like noodle dish. In Mexico, it blended European pasta with local flavors like tomatoes, chiles, and onions, becoming a distinct and beloved staple. It's a prime example of fusion cuisine done right.

Unlike soupy fideo, Fideo Seco focuses on a concentrated sauce clinging to each strand. The process involves toasting fideo in oil until golden brown, adding nutty flavor and preventing mushiness. This toasted pasta then simmers with a blended sauce of tomatoes, garlic, onion, and often chipotle for smoky depth. The result is a deeply savory, slightly spicy, comforting dish, perfect as a main or hearty side.

## Ingredients You Need
Making delicious Fideo Seco Dry Mexican Noodles requires simple, readily available ingredients. The beauty lies in humble components creating something extraordinary.
Here’s what you’ll need:
*   **Fideo Pasta:** One 7 oz (200g) package of short, thin fideo noodles. Vermicelli or angel hair pasta broken into 1-inch pieces can substitute.
*   **Tomatoes:** 3-4 ripe Roma tomatoes, quartered, or one 14.5 oz can of diced tomatoes, drained.
*   **Onion:** ½ medium white onion, roughly chopped.
*   **Garlic:** 2-3 cloves, peeled.
*   **Chicken Broth:** 3-4 cups (or vegetable broth for vegetarian).
*   **Chipotle in Adobo Sauce:** 1-2 peppers plus a teaspoon of adobo sauce. Optional, but highly recommended; adjust for desired spice level.
